Rashi on Nazir 13a:10:1.hebrew: או דילמא - אדיבורא דחבריה קאי, ומשמע כאילו אמר: ״ואני רחימנא ליה לאותו בן כוותיך, ואהא נזיר לכשיהא לך בן״. ואהא, לעיל נמי כי קא מיבעיא ליה — ״ועלי״, מאי טעמא לא מיבעיא ליה בהאי לישנא? הא לא אפשר, דלאו לישנא מתרצתא היא דלימא: ״ועלי לאוהבו כמותך״:
Rashi on Nazir 13a:10:1.english: Or perhaps - [It means that] he refers to the statement of his fellow, and it implies as though he said: "And I love that son as you [do], and I shall be a nazirite when you have a son." And regarding that [dilemma] above too, when he inquired — with regard to "And [it is incumbent] upon me," why did he not raise the dilemma with this phrasing? That is not possible, for it is not proper phrasing that one should say: "And [it is incumbent] upon me to love him as you [do]."

Rashi on Nazir 13a:10:2.hebrew: ואם תימצי לומר כל באנפיה - בין אמר ועלי, בין אמר ואני — כסיפא ליה מילתא להדורי ליה למימר: לכשיהא לי בן אהא נזיר. דאי אדעתא לקבל עליו נזירות כשיהא לו בן, למה לו להזיר בפני זה? יזיר בינו לבין עצמו! אלא, מדקאמר ליה באנפיה, איכא למימר דהכי אמר ליה: אף אני אהא נמי נזיר כשיהא לך בן:
Rashi on Nazir 13a:10:2.english: And if you say, anything in his presence - Whether he said, “And [it is] upon me,” or he said, “And I,” it is embarrassing for him to respond to him by saying, “When I have a son I will be a nazirite.” For if [it were] with the intention of accepting naziriteship upon himself when he will have a son, why does he need to take a nazirite vow in front of this person? Let him take a nazirite vow by himself! Rather, since he said it to him in his presence, it can be said that this is what he said to him: “I too will also be a nazirite when you have a son.”

Rashi on Nazir 13a:1:1.hebrew: הפילה אשתו אינו נזיר - דדילמא האי דהפילה לא הוה בן קיימא, שלא כלו לו חדשיו, ולא ולד הוי; וספק נזירות להקל:
Rashi on Nazir 13a:1:1.english: [If] his wife miscarried, he is not a nazirite - For perhaps that which she miscarried was not viable, as its months [of gestation] were not completed, and it is not [considered] an offspring; and an uncertainty regarding naziriteship is [resolved] leniently:

Rashi on Nazir 13a:1:2.hebrew: ר' שמעון אומר - אין דרך זו מוציאתו מידי נזירות:
Rashi on Nazir 13a:1:2.english: Rabbi Shimon says - This way does not release him from naziriteship.

Rashi on Nazir 13a:1:3.english: Rather, “If it was viable, I am hereby an obligatory nazirite; and if not, I am hereby a voluntary nazirite” - For he holds that [in a case of] uncertainty regarding naziriteship, [the rule is] to be stringent.

Rashi on Nazir 13a:2:1.english: [If] she gave birth again - After she miscarried.

Rashi on Nazir 13a:2:2.hebrew: הרי זה נזיר - דהשתא מיהא ולד הוא דאית ליה, וחיילא עליה נזירות:
Rashi on Nazir 13a:2:2.english: He is a nazirite - For now, at any rate, he has a child, and the naziriteship takes effect upon him.

Rashi on Nazir 13a:2:3.hebrew: ר"ש אומר - שמא הראשון הוה בן קיימא וחל עליו נזירות, והשתא כי ילדה לא חייל נזירות; ואם כדבריך יעשה, נמצא זה מביא חולין לעזרה. אלא, יחזיר וימנה נזירות שנייה, ויאמר: אם הראשון שהפילה היה בן קיימא — נזירות הראשונה חובה וזו נדבה, ואם לא היה בן קיימא — נזירות הראשונה נדבה וזו חובה:
Rashi on Nazir 13a:2:3.english: Rabbi Shimon says - Perhaps the first [fetus] was viable, and naziriteship took effect upon him, and now that she gave birth, naziriteship does not take effect. And if he acts according to your words, it turns out that he brings unconsecrated [animals] into the Temple courtyard. Rather, he should go back and count a second naziriteship, and say: "If the first [fetus] that she miscarried was viable, the first naziriteship was obligatory and this [one] is voluntary; and if it was not viable, the first naziriteship was voluntary and this [one] is obligatory."

Rashi on Nazir 13a:3:1.hebrew: האי מאי למימרא - דכי נולד לו בן, הרי זה נזיר:
Rashi on Nazir 13a:3:1.english: What is the purpose of stating this - That when a son is born to him, he is a nazirite.

Rashi on Nazir 13a:3:2.hebrew: מהו דתימא - האי דקאמר, לאו משום בן דוקא, והאי דאמר "בן" — "לכשאבנה ממנה" הוא דמשמע, כגון: "ואבנה גם אנכי ממנה" (בראשית ל), וכי נולד בת או טומטום ואנדרוגינוס נמי ליהוי נזיר — קמ"ל דלא:
Rashi on Nazir 13a:3:2.english: Lest you say - That which he said was not specifically because of a son, and that which he said "a son" means "when I will be built up through her" — as in: "that I too may be built up through her" (Genesis 30) — and when a daughter, or a tumtum, or a hermaphrodite is born, let him also be a nazirite; [the mishna therefore] teaches us that [this is] not [the case].

Rashi on Nazir 13a:4:1.hebrew: ולד דמיחשב ביני אינשי קאמינא - דהיינו בן ותו לא. קמ"ל, דבת וטומטום ואנדרוגינוס נמי איקרו ולד:
Rashi on Nazir 13a:4:1.english: I was speaking of a child that is considered significant among people - That is, a son and nothing more. [Therefore, the mishna] teaches us that a daughter, a tumtum, and a hermaphrodite are also called a child.

Rashi on Nazir 13a:5:1.hebrew: ר' יהודה - דאמר לעיל דספק נזירות להקל, כדאמרי' בפ"ק (לעיל נזיר ד' ח.), דתניא: "הריני נזיר ע"מ שיש בכרי זה ק' כור, והלך כו', ר' יהודה מתיר" — דספק נזירות להקל:
Rashi on Nazir 13a:5:1.english: Rabbi Yehuda - Who said earlier that [in a case of] uncertainty concerning naziriteship, [one rules] leniently, as we say in the first chapter (above, Nazir 8a), as it is taught [in a baraita]: "I am hereby a nazirite on condition that this heap [of grain] contains one hundred kor," and he went, etc., [and] Rabbi Yehuda permits [him], for [in a case of] uncertainty concerning naziriteship, [one rules] leniently.

Rashi on Nazir 13a:6:1.english: And he separated an offering, and she gave birth again, what is [the law] - Does it become consecrated, or not?

Rashi on Nazir 13a:7:1.hebrew: אליבא דמאן - קמיבעיא לך? אי אליבא דר"ש, פשיטא דהוי קדוש, דהאמר ספק נזירות להחמיר, וקודם שילדה אשתו נמי הוי נזיר:
Rashi on Nazir 13a:7:1.english: In accordance with whose [opinion] - is this being asked by you? If [it is] in accordance with [the opinion of] Rabbi Shimon, it is obvious that it is consecrated, for he said [that] uncertainty regarding naziriteship is [ruled] stringently, and before his wife gave birth, he was also a nazirite.

Rashi on Nazir 13a:7:2.hebrew: אלא אליבא דר' יהודה דאמר ספק נזירות להקל מאי - מי אמרינן: כיון שהפרישו בשעה שהפילה, ולא חיילא עליה נזירות כלל — לא הוי קדוש כלל, ומיבעי ליה למיהדר ולקדושי:
Rashi on Nazir 13a:7:2.english: Rather, in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, who said [that in a case of] uncertainty with regard to naziriteship [the ruling is] to be lenient, what [is the dilemma] - Do we say: Since he separated [the offering] at the time she miscarried, and naziriteship did not take effect upon him at all, it is not consecrated at all, and he must go back and consecrate [it]?

Rashi on Nazir 13a:8:1.hebrew: מאי נפקא לך מינה - אי הוה קדוש או לא, דהא ילדה וחיילא עליה נזירות:
Rashi on Nazir 13a:8:1.english: What difference does it make to you - Whether [the animal] was consecrated or not, for behold, she has [now] given birth and naziriteship has taken effect upon him.

Rashi on Nazir 13a:8:2.hebrew: נפקא מינה לגיזתו ולעבוד בו - והכי קא מיבעיא ליה: אי אמרת משעה שהפריש תחילה, כשהפילה, הוה ליה קדוש — הוה ליה אסור בגיזה ועבודה; אלא אי אמרת דלא חיילא עליה נזירות אלא משעה שחזרה וילדה — הוה ליה מותר בגיזה ובעבודה. מאי? — תיקו:
Rashi on Nazir 13a:8:2.english: The practical difference is for its shearing and for working with it - And this is what he was asking: If you say [that] from the time he initially designated [the animal], when she miscarried, it became consecrated — it would be forbidden for shearing and labor; but if you say that naziriteship did not take effect upon him until the time she gave birth again — it would be permitted for shearing and for labor. What [is the ruling]? — [The dilemma] stands [unresolved].

Rashi on Nazir 13a:9:1.hebrew: ושמע חבירו ואמר ועלי מהו אדיבוריה - דההוא גברא קאי, ומשמע: ועלי להיות נזיר כשיהיה לך בן; או דילמא אגופיה משמע — אנפשיה — דהכי משמע: ועלי נמי להיות נזיר כשיהי' לי בן:
Rashi on Nazir 13a:9:1.english: And another heard him and said, "And [it is incumbent] upon me," what is [the halakha]? "To his statement" - [Does it mean that] it refers to [the statement of] that man, and implies: "And it is [incumbent] upon me to be a nazirite when you have a son"; or perhaps it implies about his [own] body — about himself — as this is what it implies: "And it is also [incumbent] upon me to be a nazirite when I have a son"?

Tosafot on Nazir 13a:10:1.hebrew: את"ל הך אגופיה משתמע - ואיל ואמר עלי, היכא דאמר "ואני", מהו? אנפשיה קאמר — כלומר: אפי' בשאמר "ואני" אגופיה מישתמע, או דילמא "רחימנא לך כוותך" לכשיהיה בן קיימא:
Tosafot on Nazir 13a:10:1.english: "If you say this [statement] is understood about himself" - Whereas [there] he said "[And it is incumbent] upon me", where he said "And I", what is [the ruling]? Is he speaking about himself? That is to say: even when he said "And I", is it understood about himself, or perhaps [he means]: "I love you as [you love] yourself," [and will be a nazirite] when there is a viable child?

Tosafot on Nazir 13a:10:2.hebrew: את"ל כל באנפיה כסיפא ליה מילתא - דילמא מסתמא ה"ק: דרחימנא לך כוותך:
Tosafot on Nazir 13a:10:2.english: "If you say [that] whenever [it is] in his presence, the matter is embarrassing for him" - [Then] perhaps ordinarily this is what he is saying: "For I love you as you [love yourself]."

Tosafot on Nazir 13a:1:1.hebrew: הפילה אשתו - ולא ידעינן אי נפל הוא, או בן קיימא הוא וכלו לו חדשיו או שמת במעי אמו — אינו נזיר. ובגמ' מוקי לה כר' יהודה, דסבר: לא מחית איניש נפשיה לספיקא; וספק נזיר הוי — דלמא בן קיימא מה שהפילה. הלכך, טוב להתנות ולומר: "אם בן קיימא — הריני נזיר חובה מדבורי הראשון; ואם אינו בר קיימא, כגון דלא כלו לו חדשיו ולא היה בדיבורי הראשון כלום — הריני נזיר נדבה". כלומר: מעתה הריני מקבל עלי נזירות; [ומונה] נזירות ומביא קרבנותיו, ומותר ביין ומגלח. שאם לא התנה כן — כל ימיו היה מקולקל לר"ש, דמספיקא לא מצי לגלח, ויאסר כל ימיו ביין ובתגלחת ובטומאה. ור"ש לא פליג אהא דנולד לו בן טומטום וכו' — דליכא לספוקי, דכשאמר "כשיהיה לי בן" ודאי לא היה דעתו אלא לבן ודאי ולא לטומטום; ולא פליג ר"ש אלא היכא דהפילה בן זכר, דמספקא ליה דשמא הוה בן קיימא והוי בן גמור. והוא הדין דמילתיה דר"ש קאי ארישא: היכא דאמר "הריני נזיר כשיהיה לי בן" והפילה, כו':
Tosafot on Nazir 13a:1:1.english: His wife miscarried - And [even though] we do not know whether it is a non-viable fetus or a viable child whose months [of gestation] were completed, or whether it died in its mother's womb — [the Mishnah rules that] he is not a nazirite. And in the Gemara, [the Gemara] establishes this [ruling] in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, who maintains that a person does not place himself into [a state of] uncertainty; whereas [according to Rabbi Shimon,] he is in doubt whether he is a nazirite, for perhaps what she miscarried was a viable child. Therefore, it is best [for him] to stipulate and say: "If [the fetus] was viable, I am hereby an obligatory nazirite from my first statement; and if it is not viable — such as where its months [of gestation] were not completed and there was nothing to my first statement — I am hereby a voluntary nazirite." That is to say: "From now, I accept naziriteship upon myself"; and [then] he counts [a term of] naziriteship, brings his offerings, and is [then] permitted [to drink] wine and shaves [his head]. For if he did not stipulate in this manner, all his days he would be impaired according to Rabbi Shimon, because out of doubt he would not be able to shave, and he would be forbidden for all his days from wine, shaving, and [contracting corpse] impurity. And Rabbi Shimon does not disagree regarding that [ruling where] a tumtum was born to him, etc., as there is no room for doubt [there]; for when he said, "When I will have a son," his intention was certainly only for a definite son and not for a tumtum. And Rabbi Shimon disagrees only where she miscarried a male child, where it is in doubt to him whether it was perhaps a viable child and thus a full-fledged son. And the same applies [in] that Rabbi Shimon's statement refers to the first clause [of the Mishnah as well], where he said, "I am hereby a nazirite when I will have a son," and she miscarried, etc.

Tosafot on Nazir 13a:2:1.hebrew: חזרה וילדה - פי': מהריון אחר ולד קיימא. הרי זה נזיר ודאי לרבי יהודה, וילדה זו ולד קיימא; דממה שהפילה תחילה — אפי' ספק נזיר לא, וכאילו לא הפילה כלל:
Tosafot on Nazir 13a:2:1.english: "She gave birth again" - Explanation: From another pregnancy, [she gave birth to] a viable child. He is definitely a nazirite according to Rabbi Yehudah, and this birth [was of] a viable child; for regarding that which she miscarried initially, he was not even a doubtful nazirite, and [it is] as if she had not miscarried at all.

Tosafot on Nazir 13a:2:2.hebrew: רבי שמעון אומר יאמר וכו' - דלר"ש, מעת שהפילה הוי ספק נזיר; הילכך יתנה עתה בלידה זו, ויאמר: אם היה הראשון בן קיימא — נמצא שיצא נדרו מנזירות ראשון, ונזירות של לידה אחרונה נדבה; או שמא הראשון נפל היה, והנזירות הראשון נדבה היתה, ועכשיו בלידה זו מוטלת עליו נזירות של חובה, שנדר בנזיר שיהיה לו ולד. לכך צריך להתנות, דלא סגי ליה בנזירות הראשון, דשמא נדבה היתה:
Tosafot on Nazir 13a:2:2.english: "Rabbi Shimon says: He should say, etc." - For according to Rabbi Shimon, from the time [his wife] miscarried he was [in the status of] an uncertain nazirite. Therefore, he must now make a stipulation with this [subsequent] birth and say: If the first [fetus] was viable, it turns out that his vow was fulfilled through the first naziriteship, and the naziriteship of the latter birth is voluntary; or perhaps the first was a miscarriage, and the first naziriteship was voluntary, and now with this birth an obligatory naziriteship is incumbent upon him, since he vowed to be a nazirite [on condition] that he have a child. Therefore he must make a stipulation, as the first naziriteship is not sufficient for him, since perhaps it was voluntary.

Tosafot on Nazir 13a:3:1.hebrew: לכשאבנה הוא דקאמר - ולא בן ממש קאמר, אלא ל' בנין, כמו "ואבנה גם אנכי", ובכה"ג בנוי:
Tosafot on Nazir 13a:3:1.english: "He meant to say: 'When I will be built up'" - And he did not mean an actual son, but rather an expression of building, as in: "I too may be built up" [Genesis 30:3] — and in such a case [too] he is built up.

Tosafot on Nazir 13a:4:1.hebrew: ולד דחשיב ביני אינשי - דבת נמי לא מיחשבא, וכל שכן טומטום ואנדרוגינוס; קמשמע לן:
Tosafot on Nazir 13a:4:1.english: "A child that is considered [significant] among people" - [Lest you say] that even a daughter is not considered [significant], and all the more so a tumtum and a hermaphrodite; [therefore,] it teaches us [that his vow takes effect].

Tosafot on Nazir 13a:5:1.hebrew: לר' יהודה - בברייתא דאיתניא לעיל פ"ק (נזיר דף ח.) דקאמר נגנב אינו נזיר — הוא דקאמר לעיל דנזיר דכרי, דלא הוי נזיר כלל לר' יהודה. אבל לא רצה לומר ר' יהודה דהפלאה הוא, דאם כן, אפילו היה הולד בן קיימא אינו נזיר, כיון דבשעת הנדר לא היה הולד בעולם, כנ"ל:
Tosafot on Nazir 13a:5:1.english: "According to Rabbi Yehuda" - In the baraita that is taught above in the first chapter (Nazir 8a), which states that [if the heap was] stolen he is not a nazirite — that is what [the Gemara] meant above by "the nazirite of a heap [of grain]," [namely,] that according to Rabbi Yehuda he is not a nazirite at all. However, [the Gemara] did not wish to say [that our Mishnah is] Rabbi Yehuda of hafla’ah [who holds that naziriteship requires explicit specification at the time of the vow], for if so, even if the child were viable he would not be a nazirite, since at the time of the vow the child was not [yet] in the world. So it appears to me.

Tosafot on Nazir 13a:6:1.hebrew: והפילה אשתו והפריש קרבן - פי': לנזירותו. וילדה — פירוש: מאותו הריון עצמו ולד קיימא; דהשתא יש הוכחה גדולה: מדהאי בר קיימא, הנפל [הוה] נמי בר קיימא וכלו לו חדשיו, דטיפה היא נחלקת לשתים. הילכך, חלה קדושה על קרבן שהפריש כשהפילה, ששוב לא הקדיש אותם הבהמות — דאפילו לר' יהודה, דאמר לא מחית איניש נפשיה לספיקא, הכא דאיכא הוכחה גדולה, קדוש הקרבן ליאסר בגיזה ובעבודה? או דילמא, כי ה"ג דאיכא הוכחה, לר' יהודה דלא מחית איניש לספיקא, לא חלה הקדושה על הקרבן כלל מכח הפרשה ראשונה, דשמא מקצת הטיפה נקלטה מיד ומקצת הטיפה השניה לא נקלטה עד אחר שני ימים או ביום ג', וההוא נפל? (כך מסיק הש"ס ואזיל: דלר"י קמבעיא ליה; דאי אליבא דר' שמעון — הא אמר: ספק נזירות להחמיר, דבלא ילדה נמי הוי קדוש מספק, והשתא נמי כי ילדה אינו אלא ספק; אלא אליבא דר' יהודה, דאי לא ילדה — חולין הוא, והשתא כי ילדה ליה — מי הוי קדוש מספק, וכדפי'):
Tosafot on Nazir 13a:6:1.english: “And his wife miscarried, and he separated an offering” - Explanation: For his naziriteship. And [the phrase] “and she gave birth” — explanation: From that very same pregnancy, [she gave birth to] a viable child; for now there is a strong proof: Since this one is viable, the miscarried [fetus] was also viable and its months [of gestation] were completed, for it was one drop [of semen] divided into two. Therefore, did sanctity take effect upon the offering that he separated when she miscarried, such that he did not subsequently consecrate those animals [again] — for even according to Rabbi Yehuda, who says that a person does not place himself into [a state of] uncertainty, here, where there is strong proof, is the offering consecrated so as to be forbidden for shearing and for labor? Or perhaps in a case like this, where there is proof, according to Rabbi Yehuda, because a person does not place [himself] into uncertainty, the sanctity did not take effect upon the offering at all by virtue of the first separation, since perhaps part of the drop was absorbed immediately, and part of the second drop was not absorbed until after two days or on the third day, and that [miscarried one] was a non-viable fetus? (This is how the Gemara proceeds to conclude, that he is inquiring according to Rabbi Yehuda; for if [the inquiry were] according to Rabbi Shimon, doesn't he say that [in a case of] uncertainty concerning naziriteship [the rule is] to be stringent, such that even had she not given birth [the offering] would also be consecrated out of doubt, and now too, when she gave birth, it is only a doubt? Rather, [the inquiry is] according to Rabbi Yehuda, for had she not given birth, [the animal] would be unconsecrated, and now that she gave birth to [a son] for him, does it become consecrated out of doubt, as I explained.)

Tosafot on Nazir 13a:8:1.hebrew: ונפקא מינה לגיזתו ועבודתו - [ולא] דלילקי אהאי, משום דליכא כי הך סברא דולד אחרון משוי ליה בספק. דאי מספקא ליה להש"ס דשמא לילקו בודאי, מדשני בר קיימא הראשון אינו נפל — א"כ, לר' שמעון נמי מצי למיבעי למלקות: דאי לא ילדה, ליכא קדושה ודאית, אלא הוי ספק לר' שמעון; והשתא דילדה, יקדש בודאי! אלא ש"מ דלא משמע ליה להש"ס דלקי, דקדושה ודאית אין בו כי נמי ילדה, אפי' לר"ש. ע"כ הגה"ה):
Tosafot on Nazir 13a:8:1.english: "And the practical difference is for its shearing and its labor" - And [it does not mean] that one would receive lashes for this [shearing or labor], because [liability for lashes] does not apply under such reasoning that the subsequent offspring renders it [merely] in doubt. For if the Gemara were uncertain whether perhaps he should definitely receive lashes — [reasoning that] since the second [offspring] is viable, the first was [also] not a non-viable fetus — if so, [the Gemara] could have raised the dilemma according to Rabbi Shimon as well with regard to lashes: for had she not given birth [a second time], there would be no definite consecration, but rather it would be [only] an uncertainty according to Rabbi Shimon; and now that she gave birth, let it be consecrated definitely! Rather, conclude from this that the Gemara did not understand that he receives lashes, for it does not possess definite consecration even though she gave birth, even according to Rabbi Shimon. (Until here is the gloss.)

Tosafot on Nazir 13a:9:1.hebrew: ושמע חבירו ואמר ועלי - היכא דאמר "ואני ועלי", מדבוריה משתמע — כלומר: גם אני נודר בנזיר כשיהיה לי בן:
Tosafot on Nazir 13a:9:1.english: "And his fellow heard and said: 'And upon me'" - Where one said "And I, and upon me", it is implied from his speech — that is to say: "I too vow to be a nazirite when I have a son."
